removed.text:
user: Got my blood test back. HbA1c was 7.4 and the polyclinic doctor says I have type 2 diabetes too. I'm only 41.
assistant: That's a lot to take in at 41. Did the doctor talk you through a treatment plan?

user: Can you suggest a breakfast that won't spike my blood sugar? Something quick before work, since I'm diabetic now.
assistant: Try wholemeal toast with eggs, or unsweetened Greek yoghurt with nuts. Both are kinder to your blood sugar than kaya toast.

survivors.text:
user: My dad has type 2 diabetes and he keeps sneaking kueh when my mum isn't looking. How do I talk to him about it?
assistant: Gently, and without lecturing. He might listen more if his doctor explains the risks at his next check-up.

user: He's 68 and stubborn, so letting the doctor do it is probably smarter.
assistant: Probably. You could go along to the appointment and back the doctor up.

user: She wants me to walk more, so I've started doing 30 minutes after dinner around Toa Payoh.
assistant: That's a good habit to build. Evening walks are easier to stick to than you'd think.

user: I'm an accountant at a logistics firm and month-end closing keeps me at my desk 12 hours a day. How do I stay active?
assistant: Set a timer to stand every hour, take calls on your feet, and use the stairs instead of the lift.
